constraints: Flow velocity within the pipe must not exceed 1.0 m/s.
The calculated electrical input power must be 1.0 kW or less.
The selected pump's rated head at design flow must be at least 115% of the calculated Total Dynamic Head (TDH).
The selected pump's maximum electrical input rating must not exceed 1.0 kW.
The combined cost of pipe installation and pump purchase must be within a $7,500 budget.
A design is only feasible if every single constraint is satisfied; no partial compliance is allowed.
calculation_sequence: Calculate the design flow rate (Q) using daily volume and pump run hours.
For each pipe diameter (D40, D50, D63), calculate the flow velocity (v) and verify it is <= 1.0 m/s.
For each pipe diameter, calculate the friction head loss (hf) and minor head loss (hm) based on the route length.
Determine the Total Dynamic Head (TDH) by summing static head, friction head, and minor head, then calculate the required rated head (1.15 * TDH).
Calculate the electrical input power (Pin) for each pipe/TDH combination and verify it is <= 1.0 kW.
Cross-reference the required rated head and Pin against the specifications of pump options P1, P2, and P3, ensuring the pump's own max electrical rating is also <= 1.0 kW.
Compute the total installed cost (pipe length * cost per meter + pump cost) and verify it is <= $7,500.
Re-execute the hydraulic and budget calculations using the updated route length from ROUTE-V2 to determine if a feasible design still exists.
failure_modes: Velocity Constraint Violation: Selecting a pipe diameter too small leads to flow velocity exceeding 1.0 m/s.
Pump Head Insufficiency: The TDH (including the 15% margin) exceeds the rated head of all pumps that meet the electrical input constraint.
Electrical Overload: The power required to overcome the TDH exceeds the 1.0 kW limit for either the calculated input or the pump's rated maximum.
Budget Overrun: The cost of the larger diameter pipes required for velocity/head constraints combined with the necessary pump exceeds $7,500.
assumptions: The Darcy friction factor (f = 0.026) and minor loss coefficient (K = 10) remain constant across all pipe diameter options.
Pump, motor, and inverter efficiencies are uniform across all pump options provided.
Water density is constant at 1000 kg/m³.
The system operates at a steady state during the designated 5-hour daily run window.
